To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the origin of the non-thermal phenomena (radio halos and relics, HXR emission) in galaxy clusters cannot be explained by DM annihilation models.

1) the Coma cluster is not consistent with the DM interpretation of all the non-thermal phenomena; 2) the DM interpretation of non-thermal cluster phenomena is consistent only with a low neutralino DM mass and a cusp-core transition; 3) if we consider multimessenger constraints to neutralino annihilation, the possibility of interpreting non-thermal cluster observations with annihilating DM is excluded unless we introduce large boost factors due to the presence DM substructures.
DM annihilation models are not able to explain the origin of nonthermal phenomena observed in galaxy clusters, except possibly in the radio band.

, if the origin of the non-thermal phenomena of Coma is related to DM annihilation, it would require an extremely low neutralino mass (below 10 GeV) and a cored neutralino DM density profile, which would be in tension with the cosmological constraints on DM annihilation cross-sections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interpretation of non-thermal observations in terms of DM is not a straightforward task.
the origin of non thermal phenomena observed in galaxy clusters cannot be explained by annihilating DM models.

DM models with low mass neutralino and a cored density profile, if they are the only source of non-thermal emission, are ruled out by the multimessenger constraints on the neutralino annhilation cross-section.
